newsitem.title: UK: West, east Africa feature in sugar freight inquiry.
newsitem.headline: West, east Africa feature in sugar freight inquiry.

text.p: The sugar freight market saw a number of fixtures and fresh orders on Tuesday with both West and East Africa repeatedly cited as end-destinations, shipbrokers said.
Shipbrokers said CSR still had two earlier bulk orders open, for 26,000 tonnes from Queensland to China for the second half of March and 18,500 tonnes from Fiji to the UK for 1/10 April.
Of the day's new business, Czarnikow Rionda quoted for 12/14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from east coast Mexico to west or east Africa with option of Mediterranean for March/April shipment dates.
It also quoted for a further 8,500/9,000 tonnes, again in bags, from Mazatlan or Manzanillo to East or West Africa for the second half of March.
The same trade house was said to have fixed a 14,000-tonne bagged cargo from Puerto Quetzal to West Africa for prompt shipment dates.
Cargill quoted for 10,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Thailand to Kunsan for early April.

Other orders included Jean Lion with 30,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Cuba to Dubai for prompt dates and Genoc with 28/30,000 tonnes from the same origin to Baltic, Egyptian Mediterranean or Black Sea.
Shipbrokers said Sugar Chartering fixed possibly as much as 20,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from the Philippines to the U.S. for prompt dates but further details were not immediately available.
Alpine fixed 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Cuba to Casablanca at $25 with Black Sea option at $32 for 5/15 March, market sources said.
E D & F Man covered its 20,000-tonne bulk cargo from north Brazil to Casablanca or Black Sea for mid-March at around $18, they added.
In other news, China bought another cargo of Thai raw sugar for prompt shipment with Japanese trade house Mitsui named as one of the suppliers.
The vessel Feng Guang is scheduled to arrive later this month for loading and traders they expected the shipment of two more cargoes within this month.
Bangladesh has tendered on March 8 and 15 to buy one cargo of white sugar on each day.
Shipment dates have yet to be clarified although one trader said March 11/April 11 could be the period for the first tender, with shipment of the second cargo to be before April 25.
Bangladesh bought 12,500 tonnes of white sugar at its tender on March 1, again for March 11/April 11 shipment. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 8064
